newsitem.title: USA: MOF's Sakakibara denies "no rate hike" comment.
newsitem.headline: MOF's Sakakibara denies "no rate hike" comment.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, on Tuesday denied he had said Japan was not likely to raise interest rates until the end of 1996/97.
Earlier on Tuesday, a Japanese news agency quoted Sakakibara as telling a U.S. economist that Japan would not raise interest rates at least until the end of the current fiscal year ending March 31.

Asked by reporters in Washington to comment on the report, Sakakibara said: "I have not said such a thing. I've been busy here in Washington with the insurance talks (between Japan and the United States)."
Sakakibara arrived in Washington at the end of last week to attend the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank.
